label: Prostatic_Acinar_Adenocarcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma is the most common type of prostate cancer.
- Typically presents with elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels.
- Histologically characterized by acinar or glandular architecture.
- Often diagnosed through transrectal needle biopsies.
- Can metastasize to bones and lymph nodes.

## Terminology
- Prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma: A malignant tumor of the prostate with acinar or glandular architecture.

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Presence of invasive carcinoma within the prostate.
  - Acinar architecture with varying degrees of differentiation.
- **Desirable:**
  - Immunohistochemical positivity for prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP).

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Frequently associated with genetic alterations:
  - **TMPRSS2::ERG fusion**.
  - Loss of PTEN.
  - SPOP mutations.
  - ERG activation at the posttranslational level.

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Commonly affects older men, typically diagnosed in the sixth and seventh decades of life.
- **Presentation:**
  - Elevated PSA, digital rectal examination abnormalities.
  - May present with urinary symptoms.
- **Prognosis:**
  - Variable; depends on Gleason score and stage at diagnosis.
  - Can metastasize to unusual visceral metastases, including penis and testis [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/prostateprostaticduct.html).

## Microscopic
- Acinar adenocarcinoma is characterized by:
  - Malignant glands infiltrating the prostate.
  - Varying degrees of cytological atypia and architectural patterns.
  - Absence of basal cell layer.

## Ancillary Tests
- **Immunohistochemical markers:**
  - PSA and PAP: Positive in tumor cells.
- **Molecular:**
  - Common alterations include TMPRSS2::ERG fusion and PTEN loss.

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Ductal Adenocarcinoma:**
  - Papillary and cribriform architecture.
  - More aggressive clinical course than acinar adenocarcinoma.
  - [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/prostateprostaticduct.html)
  
- **Adenosquamous Carcinoma:**
  - Contains both glandular and squamous components.
  - History of radiotherapy may be present.
  - [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/GU/Adenosquamous_Carcinoma_Of_The_Prostate.html)
  
- **Mucinous (Colloid) Adenocarcinoma:**
  - Characterized by pools of extracellular mucin.
  - Similar Gleason scores to acinar adenocarcinoma.
  - [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/prostatemucinous.html)
  
- **High-Grade Prostatic Intraepithelial Neoplasia (HGPIN):**
  - Precursor lesion with crowded, stratified atypical cells.
  - Presence of basal cell layer.
  - [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/GU/High_Grade_Prostatic_Intraepithelial_Neoplasia.html)

- **Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Prostate:**
  - Defined by keratinization, keratin pearls, and intercellular bridges.
  - Absence of glandular differentiation.
  - [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/GU/Squamous_Cell_Carcinoma_Of_The_Prostate.html)
  
- **Prostatic Stromal Sarcoma:**
  - Malignant mesenchymal tumor from prostatic stroma.
  - Diffuse stromal growth with hypercellularity and atypical mitosis.
  - [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/GU/Prostatic_Stromal_Sarcoma.html)

cards.title: Prostatic cystadenoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Prostatic cystadenoma Section: microscopic Cysts are lined by a dual layer consisting of low columnar or atrophic secretory cells and flattened outer basal cells. Focal bland papillae may be seen. Cysts are surrounded by prostatic fibromuscular or fibrotic stroma, which may be hyalinized and show chronic inflammation. Squamous metaplasia may be seen in the lining epithelium. No marked epithelial atypia is present. By immunohistochemistry, the lining epithelium stains for PSA, PAP, and other prostate lineage–specific markers. Basal cells are decorated with high-molecular-weight cytokeratin and p63. Rarely, both high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia and acinar adenocarcinoma have been described as occurring in prostatic cystadenomas. Prostatic ductal adenocarcinoma can rarely present as a large multilocular mass resembling cystadenoma; however, prominent intracystic papillary growth and cytological atypia have been noted in cystadenocarcinoma.

cards.title: Adenosquamous carcinoma of the prostate
cards.excerpt: Entity: Adenosquamous carcinoma of the prostate Section: pathogenesis Most patients have a history of conventional prostatic adenocarcinoma for which they were treated by radiation and/or hormone therapy. --- The molecular background is comparable to that of conventional acinar adenocarcinoma, with TMPRSS2::ERG fusions, PTEN deletions, and SPOP mutations. In reported ERG-rearranged cases, immunohistochemical staining was strongly positive in the glandular component but weak to negative in the squamous component. One adenosquamous carcinoma with FAM131A::BRAF fusion has been reported.

cards.title: Squamous cell carcinoma of the prostate
cards.entity_name: Squamous cell carcinoma of the prostate
cards.excerpt: Entity: Squamous cell carcinoma of the prostate Section: pathogenesis ERG activation at the posttranslational level. In contrast to the morphological features of SCC, which are nonspecific with respect to the site of origin, the presence of a TMPRSS2::ERG fusion essentially confirms the prostatic origin of the carcinoma. Also typical of acinar prostatic adenocarcinoma was the loss of PTEN in 3 cases, and a PTEN mutation was identified in the remaining case.

cards.title: Prostatic cystadenoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Prostatic cystadenoma definition: Cystadenoma of the prostate is a benign epithelial neoplasm composed of multiple macroscopic cysts lined by bland prostatic secretory and basal cells and separated by fibrous or fibromuscular stroma. related_terminology: Acceptable: giant multilocular cystadenoma. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a large multiloculated cystic mass in or around the prostate gland; cysts lined by bland prostatic secretory and basal cells; no marked cytological atypia; septa with fibromuscular or fibrous stroma. Desirable: immunohistochemistry to confirm prostatic epithelial origin (if the differential diagnosis includes a seminal vesicle lesion).

cards.title: Adenoid cystic (basal cell) carcinoma of the prostate
cards.entity_name: Adenoid cystic (basal cell) carcinoma of the prostate
cards.excerpt: Entity: Adenoid cystic (basal cell) carcinoma of the prostate definition: Adenoid cystic (basal cell) carcinoma of the prostate is a malignant neoplasm thought to be derived from prostatic basal cells. related_terminology: Acceptable: adenoid cystic carcinoma; adenoid basal cell carcinoma; basal cell carcinoma of the prostate; adenoid cystic carcinoma (solid pattern). essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: basal cell morphology and immunophenotype; identification of malignant features (cytoarchitectural atypia, infiltration of non-neoplastic prostate, perineural invasion, necrosis); exclusion of metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma from a primary elsewhere, including the Cowper glands.

cards.title: High-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia
cards.excerpt: Entity: High-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia definition: High-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) is a proliferation of atypical secretory cells within prostatic glands. It is thought to be the earliest histologically recognizable precursor of invasive adenocarcinoma of the prostate. related_terminology: Acceptable: prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia. Not recommended: low-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia; grade 1, 2, or 3 prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia; carcinoma in situ. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: crowded, stratified atypical secretory cells in pre-existing normal-sized or expanded glands; enlarged, hyperchromatic, and sometimes pleomorphic nuclei; prominent nucleoli; basal layer present but often discontinuous.

cards.title: Squamous cell carcinoma of the prostate
cards.entity_name: Squamous cell carcinoma of the prostate
cards.excerpt: Entity: Squamous cell carcinoma of the prostate definition: Prostatic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a rare type of prostate cancer with squamous histology, defined by keratinization, keratin pearls, and intercellular bridges. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: squamous architecture with keratinization and/or intercellular bridges; cellular anaplasia; absence of glandular differentiation; exclusion of prostatic adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation, local invasion by bladder carcinoma with squamous features, and metastatic SCC.

cards.title: Skene gland adenocarcinoma of the urethra
cards.entity_name: Skene gland adenocarcinoma of the urethra
cards.excerpt: Entity: Skene gland adenocarcinoma of the urethra definition: Skene gland adenocarcinoma is a malignant tumour arising in female urethral accessory glands. related_terminology: Acceptable: urethral accessory gland adenocarcinoma. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a tumour with acinar to cribriform architecture and usually columnar epithelium; tumour morphology almost identical to that of prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma. Desirable: a positive reaction with prostatic immunohistochemical markers (e.g. PSA, NKX3-1).

cards.title: Ductal adenocarcinoma — Clinical features
cards.excerpt:

More likely to present with distant disease than acinar adenocarcinoma (J Urol 2010;184:2303)
Can metastasize, including to unusual visceral metastases (including penis and testis) (Cancer 2020;126:3667, Urol Oncol 2008;26:368, Am J Surg Pathol 2015;39:67, Cancer 2002;94:2610)

cards.title: Prostatic stromal sarcoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Prostatic stromal sarcoma definition: Prostatic stromal sarcoma is a malignant mesenchymal tumour that arises from the specialized prostatic stroma. related_terminology: Not recommended: cystosarcoma phyllodes. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: diffuse stromal growth with hypercellularity, cytological atypia, increased or atypical mitosis, and necrosis; sarcomatoid prostate cancer and other sarcomas should be excluded. cards.title: Ductal adenocarcinoma — Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.excerpt:
Large glands composed of tall columnar cells which often have pseudostratified nuclei
Patterns include cribriform, papillary, solid and prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia-like pattern
Cribriform: similar to acinar adenocarcinoma, cribriform pattern in ductal adenocarcinoma has been shown to be more likely to have extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, lymphovascular invasion and advanced pathologic stage (Ann Diagn Pathol 2019;39:59)
Cribriform pattern is composed of intraglandular epithelial bridging with slit-like lumens instead of the punched out lumens of cribriform acinar adenocarcinoma (Am J Surg Pathol 2011;35:615)
Papillary: true fibrovascular cores (Histopathology 2014;65:216)
Solid: often not columnar shaped (Mod Pathol 2018;31:S71)
Not specific; must see together with the other ductal patterns for diagnosis (Mod Pathol 2018;31:S71)
Prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia-like: assigned as Gleason pattern 3 (Histopathology 2012;60:59, Am J Surg Pathol 2008;32:1060)

cards.title: Ductal adenocarcinoma — Arises in primary periurethral ducts or in peripheral prostatic ducts
cards.excerpt:
Frequently is mixed with an acinar component (Virchows Arch 2013;46:429)
Most ductal adenocarcinoma is considered to be Gleason pattern 4 (5 if with comedonecrosis) (scored via the Gleason scoring system)
Cytoplasm is typically amphophilic, although it can be clear (Med Princ Pract 2010;19:82)
May have desmoplastic stromal reaction, hemorrhage, edema and inflammation (Mod Pathol 2018;31:S71)
May have intraductal spread (Mod Pathol 2018;31:S71)
Other unusual patterns that have been reported are foamy gland, Paneth cell-like neuroendocrine, micropapillary and cystic papillary (Pathology 2010;42:319)
Associated with seminal vesical invasion and less likely to be confined to the prostate than acinar adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score < 7 (Hum Pathol 2010;41:281, Virchows Arch 2013;46:429)

cards.title: Ductal adenocarcinoma — CK7, CK20 (can be patchy positive); typically negative for CDX2
cards.excerpt:
Molecular / cytogenetics description
PTEN loss by IHC was less frequent compared with pure acinar carcinoma; TMPRSS2::ERG gene fusion is infrequent (Mod Pathol 2009;22:359, Prostate 2015;75:1610)
PTEN, RB1 and TP53 alterations, in a case report of ductal adenocarcinoma having neuroendocrine phenotype (BMC Med Genomics 2021;14:245)
Low rates of ERG rearrangement by IHC and FISH (Prostate 2015;75:1610)
Considerable gene expression overlap with acinar adenocarcinoma; however, early research suggests that prolactin receptor protein is overexpressed in ductal (compared to acinar) adenocarcinoma (Mod Pathol 2009;22:1273)
High percentage of DNA damage repair pathway alterations (JCO Precis Oncol 2019;3:PO.18.00327)
Often the genomic profile is similar to castration resistant prostatic acinar adenocarcinoma (Nat Rev Urol 2021;18:337)
MAP3K1 homozygous deletion (case report) (IJU Case Rep 2021;4:176)
Most often are clonally related, in cases of mixed acinar and ductal adenocarcinoma (Prostate 2022;82:576)
Aneuploidy (Prostate 2022;82:576)

cards.title: Adenosquamous carcinoma — Essential features
cards.excerpt:
Adenosquamous prostatic carcinoma is a very rare aggressive tumor
Critical to exclude other sources of the squamous component through clinical history, examinations, endoscopy and immunostains
67% of cases are associated with prior androgen deprivation therapy or radiotherapy
Diagnosis requires proper morphology and immunostaining with prostate specific markers (prostate specific antigen [PSA], prostate specific membrane antigen [PSMA], prostatic specific acid phosphatase [PSAP] and prostatic acid phosphatase [PAP]), which should be positive in the glandular and negative in the squamous component

cards.title: Adenosquamous carcinoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Theories
Metaplastic transformation of adenocarcinoma frequently after treatment; this is supported by a case of adenosquamous carcinoma in which the squamous component rose from 5% before adjuvant radiotherapy to predominantly squamous after radiotherapy (Eur J Cancer 2018;95:109)
Collision tumor: intermingling of squamous and glandular components with no abrupt transition argues against this, as does the observation that squamous component may be PSAP reactive (Hum Pathol 1984;15:87, Int J Urol 2005;12:319, Scientific World Journal 2006;6:2491)
Arises from pluripotent stem cells capable of multidirectional differentiation (Urol Case Rep 2019;29:101084)

cards.title: Adenosquamous carcinoma — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
No standard therapy and it depends on details
Radical prostatectomy (Rare Tumors 2010;2:e47)
Radical cystoprostatectomy due to bladder neck involvement, androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and radiation with survival (Urol Case Rep 2019;29:101084)

Radiation plus androgen deprivation with survival in 1 of 2 cases (Scand J Urol Nephrol 1994;28:425)
Enzalutamide then carboplatin (Int Urol Nephrol 2023;55:613)

cards.title: Mucinous (colloid) adenocarcinoma — Radiology description
cards.excerpt:

cards.title: Mucinous (colloid) adenocarcinoma — Prognostic factors
cards.excerpt:
2 most authoritative studies found no statistically significant difference with conventional adenocarcinoma; thus, mucinous and nonmucinous cancer seem to have an equivalent biological potential
In the first amassed 14 cases from a database of > 3,600, median overall follow up of 6.4 years (Urology 2006;68:825)
Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database study apparently confirmed a similar outcome (Front Oncol 2020;9:1467)
An additional study showed organ confined or locally advanced mucinous carcinoma was not different in outcome from all adenocarcinomas but 5 year survival was worse in the metastatic state for mucinous (26% versus 84%) (Int J Cancer 2025;156:2311)
One study confirmed that 5 year biochemical recurrence rates were not significantly different from nonmucinous cases (Histopathology 2017;71:641)

cards.title: Mucinous (colloid) adenocarcinoma — Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.excerpt:
Primary mucinous (colloid) adenocarcinoma of the prostate is defined as prostatic adenocarcinoma with pools of extracellular mucin involving 25% or more of the entire tumor
If mucin is < 25% of the resected tumor mass, this is designated as adenocarcinoma with mucinous features (Urology 2006;68:825)
The latter term is also preferred when the lesion is identified on biopsy or transurethral resection since the entire prostate is not available to confirm the percentage that is mucinous (Mod Pathol 2018;31:S80)
Grade the tumor according to underlying architecture; most are Gleason 4 (Am J Surg Pathol 2016;40:244, Histopathology 2017;71:641)
Most common mucin secreting pattern, however, was Gleason grade 3, which usually showed distinctive luminal distention

cards.excerpt:

Young age at presentation (Am J Surg Pathol 2003;27:1523)
Involvement of peripheral zone of the prostate (Am J Surg Pathol 2003;27:1523)

Perineural and periglandular invasion (Am J Surg Pathol 2003;27:1523)
Metastatic disease (present in 15 - 20% of cases, with 50% mortality) (Am J Surg Pathol 2003;27:1523, Am J Surg Pathol 2004;28:1289, Am J Surg Pathol 2007;31:697)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic (basal cell) carcinoma — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Limited data to determine optimal treatment due to rarity of the entity
Transurethral resection or prostatectomy has been a treatment option used for patients with localized disease (Curr Oncol 2022;29:1866)
Advanced cases may benefit from radiotherapy or chemotherapy (Curr Oncol 2022;29:1866, Urol Case Rep 2022;42:102025)

cards.title: Nephrogenic metaplasia / adenoma — Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.excerpt:
Tubules lined by simple cuboidal, flattened or hobnail cells, forming an exophytic papillary or endophytic lesion (Urology 2016;95:29)
Associated acute and chronic inflammation and edema in the stroma; lack of desmoplastic reaction
Many morphologic variants (multiple patterns may occur in the same cases): papillary, tubular, tubulocystic, polypoid, flat, fibromyxoid, signet ring cell-like (Mod Pathol 2013;26:792)
Hyaline rim surrounds the tubules (PAS positive thickened basement membrane) (Adv Anat Pathol 2019;26:171)
